title: SLO-driven pricing and cache strategy - Kalypso Financial intake
summary: Initial discovery focused on balancing latency SLOs with per-token cost. Kalypso is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for a payments fraud scoring feature. Team requested detailed pilot pricing, security docs, and a micro-benchmark plan using their sample traces.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-10 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SE), Noah Reed (Redwood SA); Priya Nair (Head of ML - Kalypso), Daniel Brooks (Platform Eng), Avery Stone (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Discussed economics of per-token pricing vs dedicated capacity; explored caching, batching, and routing levers to hit 99th percentile latency targets while staying inside pilot budget.

[00:00:03] Ethan Park: Hey everyone; thanks for joining, we'll kick off, I'm Ethan from Redwood, my teammate Sofia is our SE, Noah is our solutions architect. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Priya Nair: Good thanks, Priya here. Appreciate you making time, we've been looking at Redwood's docs and want to validate cost and latency for a fraud scoring use-case.
[00:00:18] Avery Stone: Hi, Avery - PM - quick note on timeline: we want a pilot in the next 6 weeks ideally.
[00:00:25] Daniel Brooks: Daniel, platform. Main thing for us is data residency and whether we can run in our VPC for compliance. Also curious about cost profile.
[00:00:32] Sofia Alvarez: Great - thanks. Our goal for this call is to understand your SLOs, workload shape, and constraints so we can suggest hosted vs dedicated vs private and sizing plus batching/caching levers.
[00:00:44] Ethan Park: Quick ask — can you summarize the call pattern? average tokens per request, percent short vs long?
[00:00:50] Priya Nair: Typical request is a short prompt, 20-40 tokens, but we'll have longer follow-ups in some flows. Peak qps is small today — 15-20 rps — but we expect bursty spikes up to 150 rps during batch jobs.
[00:01:03] Daniel Brooks: And we need p99 under 120ms for the short prompts; p95 ideally below 60ms.
[00:01:08] Noah Reed: Okay, those are tight SLOs for a generative model path. Two immediate levers: 1) Use prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts which reduces compute and latency; 2) Batching helps throughput but increases single-request latency. We'll talk through tradeoffs.
[00:01:25] Priya Nair: Can you quantify the unit cost differences? We saw your per-token hosted rates but want a realistic per-inference number with caching.
[00:01:33] Sofia Alvarez: Sure — rough calc off the cuff: hosted per-token rates depend on model family; with heavy KV caching and short prompts you can drive effective per-inference cost down significantly. Example: a 30-token prompt with 64 token response on a medium open model might cost X cents hosted; but with prefix cache hit rate at 60% we could drop compute per request by ~40-50%. We'll send a worksheet.
[00:01:56] Avery Stone: When you say cache, is that KV cache on the GPU, or something persisted?
[00:02:02] Noah Reed: Good q — KV cache is GPU-resident during the session for autoregressive decoding. We also offer prefix caching (server-side) to cache embeddings/prefix computations for repeated prompts across sessions — that's persisted at the infra layer and can hit many requests. There's also a lightweight HTTP-edge cache for identical prompts.
[00:02:20] Daniel Brooks: If we use Redwood-hosted with prefix cache, does our data leave region? We need US-only residency.
[00:02:27] Ethan Park: We can pin region on hosted and provide US-only hosts; for strict compliance we have Dedicated or Private (VPC) options that keep data within your VPC/network. We'll share the region residency guarantees and the private deployment checklist.
[00:02:42] Priya Nair: How does dedicated compare cost-wise vs hosted? We're sensitive to unit cost under the pilot cap.
[00:02:47] Sofia Alvarez: Dedicated is fixed capacity — you pay for reserved GPU pools. Unit cost depends on utilization. If you're fully utilizing the pool, dedicated per-token cost can be lower than hosted. But with low-utilization or spiky traffic, hosted with intelligent routing + burst capacity often wins. We'll run scenarios.
[00:03:03] Avery Stone: So we need a tradeoff model — if we're at 20 rps steady vs 150 rps spikes, what's the expected burn?
[00:03:09] Noah Reed: We'll model steady utilization vs burst. Two knobs: autoscale/burst for dedicated and routing to cheaper model variants during non-critical windows. Also token slicing: you can truncate or use shorter context for non-critical queries.
[00:03:22] Priya Nair: Token slicing — can you explain? Sounds like we're dropping tokens and impacting model quality.
[00:03:27] Sofia Alvarez: It's selective trimming. For scoring short prompts we usually don't need long context; for longer threads we preserve essential tokens. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and token-slicing profiles per workload.
[00:03:39] Daniel Brooks: Any latency penalty for prefix cache misses?
[00:03:43] Noah Reed: Misses mean you pay full compute and warm the KV; first request is slower but subsequent ones are faster. We also offer warm-up APIs to prepopulate caches if you know traffic patterns.
[00:03:53] Ethan Park: A realistic pilot approach: start hosted, run sample traffic for 24-72 hrs, measure p95/p99, then evaluate dedicated sizing if steady-state utilization justifies committed capacity.
[00:04:03] Priya Nair: That fits our timeline. Pilot budget: we have a $25k cap for the pilot. Can you run a model to show whether hosted will fit?
[00:04:12] Sofia Alvarez: Yes — we'll back-of-envelope first, then precise after we get traces. If your average tokens per inference are low and cache hit rate is decent, $25k often covers a two-week stress run on hosted. Dedicated would need commitment and an up-front minimum.
[00:04:27] Avery Stone: What about quantization? We read about 4-bit options — does Redwood support that and does it break quality?
[00:04:33] Noah Reed: We support quantized execution paths and post-quant evals. 4-bit can reduce cost significantly with small quality delta on some models, but you need to validate on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per model and workload.
[00:04:48] [00:04:48] Daniel Brooks: On security: we need KMS integration, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and retention controls. Are those supported on hosted?
[00:04:55] Ethan Park: Hosted supports per-customer encryption, but for full KMS/HSM integration and account-level SSO we recommend Dedicated or Private. We do offer enterprise features on hosted too—will share SOC2 docs and the KMS integration matrix.
[00:05:07] Priya Nair: For the bench plan, what telemetry should we collect?
[00:05:11] Sofia Alvarez: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens generated, batch sizes, successful vs retried requests, GPU utilization, memory pressure, prefix cache hit rate, and per-model cost breakdown. We want your sample traces plus any spike traces.
[00:05:24] Avery Stone: We'll add those. Daniel will export sample traffic.
[00:05:27] Daniel Brooks: Yep will send 24hr traces with token histogram. Anything else?
[00:05:31] Noah Reed: One nuance: batching tradeoff — if you want strict p99 under 120ms you generally need to bound batching windows (e.g., max 1–2ms queue time) which reduces batching efficiency. We can show sensitivity curves.
[00:05:45] Priya Nair: Can Redwood do canary routing? For certain flows we want to route 10% to a cheaper model variant and fall back on quality failures.
[00:05:52] Ethan Park: Yes, routing policies and automatic fallback are supported; you can route by policy (latency, cost, region) and do A/B or canary rollouts.
[00:06:00] Avery Stone: Pricing ask — can you provide a simple per-inference example for our short prompts with 50% prefix cache hits?
[00:06:05] Sofia Alvarez: We'll prepare a simple sheet: inputs — tokens in prompt/response, cache hit rate, model family, and we'll produce hosted per-inference cost and a dedicated utilization-based rate.
[00:06:16] Daniel Brooks: Any minimums for dedicated? NRE or setup costs?
[00:06:19] Ethan Park: There's a ramp: reserved capacity has monthly commit and setup for networking. For Private (VPC) there's an onboarding project and a small integration fee. We'll outline those in the pricing doc.
[00:06:31] Priya Nair: Quality concerns — if we quantize and use cheaper model variants will we lose too much accuracy for fraud scoring? We need low false positives.
[00:06:39] Noah Reed: That's why benchmark on your labeled data is critical. We'll run the same prompts through candidate models and quantization levels and report delta on your metrics (AUC, FPR at fixed TPR).
[00:06:52] [00:06:52] Avery Stone: Good. Can you also include an example of how token caching reduces cost for repeated user sessions?
[00:06:58] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, an example table and a small simulation — e.g., 60% prefix hit reduces average compute per-inference by ~45%, subject to prompt shape.
[00:07:10] Priya Nair: On SLA — what's your uptime SLA for hosted vs dedicated?
[00:07:15] Ethan Park: Hosted has a standard SLA; Dedicated has stronger SLA tiers with enterprise SLAs for latency targets if you go with a supported commit. We'll include precise SLO language.
[00:07:24] Daniel Brooks: For the bench run — do you need us to open ports or provide credentials?
[00:07:28] Noah Reed: For hosted benchmark, no infra changes: you'll provide traces and we replay against our endpoints. For VPC/private pilot, we need networking details and a short onboarding. We'll include a checklist.
[00:07:39] Avery Stone: Excellent. Next steps?
[00:07:41] Ethan Park: I'll share the pricing worksheet and SOC2 + KMS doc by Tuesday. Sofia will draft the micro-benchmark plan and Noah will add the network/private checklist. Daniel will send traces. Priya will confirm the pilot success criteria (latency and allowed cost per inference).
[00:07:56] Priya Nair: Confirmed. We'll aim to get traces to you by Monday.
[00:08:00] Ethan Park: Great—let's lock a bench session for week of July 20. I'll send a calendar invite. Thanks everyone.
[00:08:06] [crosstalk briefly]
[00:08:10] Daniel Brooks: Quick Q — what about audit logs granularity? We need per-token request-level logs for forensics.
[00:08:15] Ethan Park: We can provide request-level logs with redaction options under enterprise controls; will include examples in docs.
[00:08:22] Avery Stone: Perfect. Anything else?
[00:08:25] Priya Nair: No — that's it from us, thanks.
[00:08:28] Ethan Park: Awesome. We'll follow up.

[End of transcript — remainder of meeting notes and some follow-ups recorded in the CRM]
